item.title: Safety and accuracy diverge across deployment conditions in clinical large language models
item.description: Clinical large language models (LLMs) are commonly scaled by increasing model size, context length, retrieval complexity, or inference-time compute, on the assumption that higher accuracy implies safer behavior. In medicine, where a few confident or evidence-contradicting errors can outweigh average performance, this assumption may be incomplete. item.description: Conversational agents (CAs) increasingly guide, support, and monitor people through sustained dialogue, yet AI leadership research has mostly examined reactions to AI framed as a leader, not the influence behaviors such agents enact. item.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
item.description: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. item.title: Fare Calculation Methodology in Automated Public Transport Payment Systems: Zoning, Per-kilometer, and Adaptive Tariffs
item.description: The purpose of the research is to develop proposals for tariff setting in automated fare collection systems for public transport. item.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
item.description: Artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology whose development requires coordinated institutional, regulatory, ethical, and infrastructural governance.
